hints: Think about where the acidity in rain actually comes from, which gases dissolve to make acids.
Statement 1 is true because $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{NO}_2$ both react with water to give acidic solutions, and statement 2 is true because acid dissolves metal compounds from rocks and soil.
Check statement 3 by remembering how $\text{NO}_2$ can oxidise $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ and then be reformed, which is the definition of catalysis.
walkthrough:
**Check Statement 1 - Formation of Acids**

Think simply, acid rain means rain more acidic than normal. That acidity comes from non-metal oxides dissolving.

Chemical idea:
$$\text{SO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$$
$$2\text{NO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HNO}_2 + \text{HNO}_3$$

**Check Statement 2 - Leaching of Heavy Metals**

Acid is great at dissolving things. When acidic water flows over rocks, soil and lake beds, it reacts with insoluble metal compounds.

This releases ions such as $\text{Al}^{3+}$, $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cd}^{2+}$ into rivers and lakes, which harms aquatic life. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check Statement 3 - Catalytic Role of NO2**

In the atmosphere, $\text{SO}_2$ is oxidised slowly by oxygen, but $\text{NO}_2$ speeds this up and is regenerated.

Catalytic cycle:
$$\text{NO}_2 + \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \text{NO} + \text{SO}_3$$
$$\text{NO} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{NO}_2$$

Because $\text{NO}_2$ is reformed, it acts as a catalyst. So statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the Conclusions**

All three statements, 1, 2 and 3, are correct. So you choose the option that includes 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. Oxides of N and S form acids with water, acid leaches heavy metal ions into water courses, and NO2 catalyses oxidation of SO2 to SO3.
options.B: False. This option omits statement 3. Many students doubt statement 3 because they only remember V2O5 as the catalyst in the Contact process, but in the atmosphere NO2 does catalyse SO2 to SO3.
options.C: False. This option omits statement 1. Statement 1 is the basic definition of acid rain formation, so it cannot be left out.
options.D: False. This option includes only statement 1. It misses the environmental effect in statement 2 on metal leaching and the catalytic chemistry in statement 3.
